skill.name: frontend-design
skill.description: Create distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces with intentional aesthetics, high craft, and non-generic visual identity. Use when building or styling web UIs, components, pages, dashboards, or frontend applications.
skill.summary: Guides AI agents to build distinctive, production-ready frontend interfaces with clear design direction.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: All static findings appear to be false positives in a Markdown-only design instruction file. The backtick findings are fenced Markdown examples, and the reconnaissance findings are design language about typography, color, layout, and motion. No evidence of command execution, prompt injection, data exfiltration, or malicious intent was found.

static_findings.snippet: * Avoid system fonts and AI-defaults (Inter, Roboto, Arial, etc.)

finding_verdicts.reason: Lines 61-63 are a fenced Markdown block showing the DFII scoring formula, not Ruby or shell backtick execution. No command invocation or user-controlled execution path is present.
The detected backticks are Markdown fence syntax around documentation text. They do not define or execute an external command.
The line says to avoid generic AI UI patterns as design guidance. It contains no system probing, host enumeration, or reconnaissance behavior.
The phrase system fonts refers to visual typography choices, not computer system reconnaissance. The instruction is limited to frontend design style.
The line advises against evenly balanced color palettes. It is aesthetic guidance and does not request any environment inspection.
Break the grid intentionally is a layout composition instruction. It does not reference operating system, network, or filesystem reconnaissance.
The line warns against decorative micro-motion in UI animation. It is frontend design guidance with no security-sensitive behavior.

content.value_statement: Generic AI-generated interfaces make products look interchangeable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward crafted UI direction, design systems, and working frontend code.
actual_capabilities: Defines an explicit aesthetic direction before implementation.
Scores design ideas with the DFII framework.
Specifies typography, color, spacing, and motion choices.
Guides production-ready HTML, CSS, React, or animation output.
Checks work against anti-patterns for generic AI UI.
limitations: Does not include packaged design assets or component files.
Requires product context to choose the best visual direction.
Does not replace accessibility testing in real browsers.
Focuses on frontend presentation, not backend application logic.

use_cases.title: Create a Product Interface
use_cases.description: Turn a rough web app idea into a distinctive first screen with clear visual direction and working frontend structure.

use_cases.title: Refresh a Generic UI
use_cases.description: Replace default layouts, fonts, and colors with a cohesive design system that fits the product audience.

use_cases.title: Shape a Design Brief
use_cases.description: Compare aesthetic directions, score feasibility, and define implementation rules before building components.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Page
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner prompt for a single interface.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a production-ready landing page for [product]. Choose one clear aesthetic direction, define the design system, and implement the first screen.

prompt_templates.title: Improve an Existing UI
prompt_templates.prompt: Redesign this interface to avoid generic AI UI patterns. Keep the core workflow, but improve typography, color, layout, and motion.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Component System
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for reusable frontend design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a frontend design system for [application type]. Include aesthetic direction, reusable component rules, accessibility expectations, and implementation guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Evaluate and Build Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced prompt for design strategy and execution.
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare three visual directions for [product], score each with DFII, choose the strongest option, then build the interface using that direction.

output_examples.input: Build a dashboard for an operations team that should feel precise, fast, and serious.
output_examples.output: The response would define an industrial utilitarian direction, specify typography and layout rules, then provide a working dashboard implementation.

output_examples.input: Redesign a generic SaaS homepage so it feels memorable and premium.
output_examples.output: The response would replace default patterns with a focused visual thesis, refined type choices, restrained color, and purposeful motion.

output_examples.input: Choose a visual style for a playful finance education app.
output_examples.output: The response would compare several directions, score them with DFII, and recommend the most suitable design before implementation.

best_practices: Provide audience, product goal, and desired emotional tone before asking for implementation.
Ask for the DFII score when comparing multiple visual directions.
Validate the generated interface for accessibility, responsiveness, and performance.
anti_patterns: Asking for a beautiful UI without product context or target users.
Mixing too many aesthetics in one interface.
Accepting default fonts, colors, and layouts without review.

faq.question: What does this skill help create?
faq.answer: It helps create distinctive frontend interfaces, design systems, and working web UI implementations.

faq.question: Can it work with React?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes React guidance and can also support HTML, CSS, and animation-focused work.

faq.question: Does it generate production-ready code?
faq.answer: It instructs the agent to produce clean, accessible, modular frontend code suitable for production review.

faq.question: Is it only for landing pages?
faq.answer: No. It can support dashboards, components, application screens, product pages, and design refreshes.

faq.question: Does it choose fonts and colors?
faq.answer: Yes. It asks the agent to define typography, color variables, spacing, and motion rules.

faq.question: What should I provide in my prompt?
faq.answer: Provide the product purpose, audience, brand tone, target workflow, and any technical constraints.
